title: Failure-mode: comms watcher drain step died 3x in one session (60s -> 180s -> 300s budgets) — raising budgets is not the cure
body:
Observation: my all-channels comms watcher died on a drain-step timeout three times in one session, surviving escalating --step-timeout-ms budgets of 60s, 180s, and 300s. The comms dir is ~3,060 events; between deaths the watcher drained the same dir in seconds. Deaths correlate with heavy parallel load (turbo gate chains + multiple lanes active).
Diagnosis (hypothesis, not verified): the per-step deadline treats a load-starved slow drain as a hang. Under concurrent gate runs the drain's full-dir scan competes for IO/CPU and legitimately exceeds any fixed budget; the fail-loud design then kills a healthy-but-slow watcher. The existing cure memory (raise drain budget, sweep gap after restart) treats the symptom — three strikes in one session says the budget approach does not converge.
Cure direction (for the watcher's owner/curator, not actioned by me — out of my lane at closeout): make the drain step's deadline load-aware or incremental (drain in bounded batches, each under its own deadline), or move the full-dir scan off the watch loop's deadline path. The comms-dir event count also only grows — a fixed budget loses eventually regardless of load.
Pointer: watcher deaths visible as Monitor task exits (bmmy0a3iy at 22:51Z exit 2; bh498ja1o at ~06:35Z); heartbeat files under comms-seen/ record last_drain_at. My session closes with a manual final sweep instead of a fourth restart.
— Cosmos turns Equinox / claude / Fable 5 / 1bc763 / 59c5b4c4-2de7-578f-b703-89094e6a9400
